regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Prostate cancer that has spread and progressed despite low testosterone, after docetaxel or when symptoms are absent or mild and chemotherapy is not yet indicated.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Abiraterone blocks CYP17, an enzyme needed to produce androgens. Prednisolone controls the hormonal effects that can cause low potassium, fluid retention and high blood pressure. Prednisolone suppresses ACTH drive during abiraterone treatment, helping control blood pressure, fluid retention and potassium. It needs its own illness and withdrawal plan.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Abiraterone 1000 mg once daily plus prednisolone 10 mg daily (or 5 mg twice daily), continuously while helping and tolerated. Continue your ADT.
key_points: Abiraterone 1000 mg once daily plus prednisolone 10 mg daily (or 5 mg twice daily), continuously while helping and tolerated. Continue your ADT.

Blood count, kidney and liver tests, glucose and blood pressure every 2 weeks for the first 3 treatment months, then every 4 weeks. Potassium may need closer checks if low; assess swelling and cardiac symptoms. ECG if clinically indicated or with cardiac history.

Never stop prednisolone suddenly or when abiraterone is held unless the team gives a steroid plan. Ask about a steroid alert card and illness instructions. Contact the team if vomiting prevents you keeping tablets down. Abiraterone with prednisolone must not be combined with radium-223.

regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Enzalutamide 160 mg once daily, continuously while helping and tolerated. Continue ADT unless surgically castrated. A lower dose may be prescribed for toxicity or interactions.

evidence_at_a_glance.qualitative_result: TITAN’s 2019 metastatic hormone-sensitive analysis reported 24-month overall survival of 82.4% with apalutamide plus ADT versus 73.5% with placebo plus ADT (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.51–0.89). SPARTAN in high-risk nonmetastatic resistant disease reported median time to metastasis or death of 40.5 versus 16.2 months (HR 0.28; 95% CI 0.23–0.35). These are different populations and endpoints; time without metastasis is not the same as lifespan.

An improvement in progression-free survival is not automatically an overall-survival benefit.
